title: Tenant Key Escrow, Rotation & SIEM Playbook
content:
Purpose
This playbook documents an operational pattern for tenant key escrow, HSM-backed BYOK key onboarding, automated rotation procedures, and SIEM export mappings. It ties KMS/HSM lifecycle actions to RBAC v2 controls and to a reproducible evidence package for audits.

Scope
- Applies to: Redwood-hosted KMS endpoints and private deployment control planes where customer-managed keys (BYOK) are allowed.
- Excludes: ephemeral session keys used only inside single-request flows and third-party managed keys outside our control plane.

Goals
1) Provide a repeatable, auditable process for bringing tenant keys into HSM-backed vaults (escrow and import).
2) Define a safe rotation model (scheduled and emergency) with minimum service disruption and evidence artifacts.
3) Specify the audit log schema and SIEM export mappings so detection and compliance reporting are robust.
4) Integrate RBAC v2 constraints so key operations are authorized and least-privilege.

High-level architecture & key concepts
- KEK/DEK envelope pattern: Customer DEKs (data encryption keys) are wrapped by KEKs (key encryption keys) stored in an HSM. Our KMS issues DEKs to services; DEKs never persist unwrapped in storage.
- HSM-backed KEKs: Root KEKs live in hardware modules (FIPS 140-2/3 level documented per deployment). Import uses secure key import tokens and attestation artifacts.
- Escrow: For BYOK, tenants may supply a key-encrypting blob that is imported into HSM or escrowed using an escrow agent. Escrow includes an import manifest, attestation quote, and signature by the tenant.
- RBAC v2 integration: All key management operations are gated by RBAC v2 roles and policies mapped to service accounts and human principals.

RBAC v2 patterns for KMS/HSM access
- Roles to define: kms-admin (create/delete/import), kms-operator (rotate/backup), kms-audit (read audit logs), kms-usage (encrypt/decrypt only), escrow-manager (onboard BYOK artifacts).
- Role bindings: prefer service-principal bindings for apps, short-lived token for humans, and MFA+approval for critical ops (key deletion, export).
- Policy examples (conceptual):
  - deny key-deletion unless two approvals from kms-admin + escrow-manager within 24h window.
  - allow key-wrap for service-principal with scope limited to specific tenant-id and route.
- Enforcement: RBAC decision is evaluated at API gateway before KMS endpoint; denial returns structured error code KMS-RBAC-403.

Audit log schema (canonical JSON event)
Field list (all events emitted for key ops):
- event_ts: ISO-8601 timestamp in UTC
- event_id: UUIDv4
- actor_type: user | service | system
- actor_principal: display name or service id (string)
- actor_id: internal principal id (opaque string)
- tenant_id: tenant identifier
- action: encrypt | decrypt | import_key | rotate_key | schedule_rotation | delete_key | get_key_metadata | attest_import
- key_id: canonical key id (ke-...)
- key_version: version tag (vYYYYMMDD-HHMMSS)
- operation_result: success | failure
- error_code: optional short code (e.g., KMS-403-RBAC, KMS-409-KEY-IN-USE)
- source_ip: IP address of the caller (if available)
- request_id: correlation id used across stack
- duration_ms: operation latency
- hsm_attestation: boolean true/false or base64 quote id when present
- evidence_artifact: reference id for stored artifact bundle (if created)

Note: Logs MUST avoid storing plaintext key material. If an HSM quote or import blob reference is recorded, it must be to a secure artifact store with restricted ACLs and a digest only included in the log (sha256).

SIEM export mapping and parsing guidance
- Export format: canonical JSON events forwarded over TLS to the SIEM ingestion endpoint. For Splunk, use HTTP Event Collector; for Elastic, use Beats/Logstash adapter.
- Field mappings to common schemas: map tenant_id -> ecs.project or ecs.customer, event_ts -> @timestamp, actor_id -> user.id, request_id -> trace.id, key_id -> kafka.key_id (or custom field).
- Example event (single-line JSON):
  {"@timestamp":"2026-02-19T18:24:03Z","event_id":"8f2a1b3c-...","actor_type":"service","actor_id":"svc-auth-proxy-12","tenant_id":"tn-5101","action":"import_key","key_id":"ke-tn-5101-0007","operation_result":"success","hsm_attestation":true,"evidence_artifact":"evid-20260219-0007","request_id":"req-9b3c"}
- Parser notes: SIEM ingestion should extract key_id, tenant_id, action, operation_result, and request_id as indexed fields for rapid search. Also extract hsm_attestation and evidence_artifact for compliance workflows.

Detection rules (SIEM) – suggested starting set
- Unauthorized key deletion attempts: action == delete_key AND operation_result == failure AND error_code == KMS-403-RBAC => high_alert
- Unusual rotation frequency: repeated rotate_key events for same key_id exceeding configured threshold within 24 hours => medium_alert
- HSM attestation failure: action in {import_key, attest_import} AND hsm_attestation == false => high_alert + paging
- Escrow download spike: many escrow manifest downloads for a tenant within short window => investigate for data-exfil

Evidence automation and artifact package
- Evidence package contents (for each rotation or import):
  - operation manifest (JSON): fields describing operation, actor, timestamps, request_ids
  - signed attestation quote (HSM) or import receipt (base64)
  - RBAC approval log snapshot (signed by approvers)
  - Audit log slice (ndjson) covering the operation window
  - Checksum file (sha256sums)
  - Human-readable summary (markdown)
- Packaging: artifact is generated by the KMS control plane and stored in the evidence-bucket with ACLs restricted to kms-audit role and legal. The audit log will include the artifact id and the sha256 for later verification.
- Automation triggers: scheduled rotation completion, manual onboarding, emergency rotate. Each trigger results in generation and retention of evidence package.

Key rotation procedures (scheduled and emergency)
1) Pre-rotation checks (automated):
   - Verify no outstanding long-lived sessions tied to DEKs (session_count metric)
   - Confirm backup snapshot of metadata is stored and replicated
   - Run a simulation of rewrap on a test prefix using new KEK (dry-run)
2) Rotation steps (automated preferred):
   - Create new KEK version in HSM (import or generate inside HSM)
   - Generate rotation manifest containing key_version, ke_kid, expected impact window, request_id
   - Rewrap DEKs: call rewrap api which atomically wraps each tenant DEK with new KEK; rewrap is implemented as streaming re-encryption with KV cache invalidation
   - Emit rotation-complete event and generate evidence package
   - Mark old KEK for scheduled destruction after retention period (default 90 days)
3) Post-rotation validation:
   - Smoke encrypt/decrypt cycles for representative tenants
   - Dashboard: show rewrap success ratio, latency percentiles, and error rate per tenant
4) Emergency rotation (compromise suspected):
   - Lock key_id (deny further encrypt/decrypt) via RBAC policy change and force deny flag
   - Generate new KEK immediately and start rewrap for high-priority prefixes only (tiered fallback)
   - Create legal/compliance incident artifact and page responders
   - If proof-of-compromise confirmed, schedule immediate destruction of compromised key version after evidence snapshot created

Operational safeguards & metrics
- Metrics to monitor: rotation_success_rate, rewrap_error_rate, avg_wrap_latency_ms, hsm_queue_depth, attest_failures_count, key_delete_attempts, escrow_downloads_per_tenant
- SLOs: 99.9% rotation success for scheduled rotations within defined window; rewrap latency p50 < 200ms per object in streaming path.
- Alerts: page on hsm_attestation failures > 3 in 1 hour or rotation_success_rate < 95% for a scheduled run.

Onboarding BYOK (tenant-facing steps)
1) Tenant requests BYOK via console API; system returns import-token and temporary upload location.
2) Tenant produces a wrapped KEK blob using recommended toolchain and provides attestation and public metadata.
3) Escrow-manager role validates manifest, verifies attestation quote, and triggers import_job.
4) After import, KMS emits import_key event with hsm_attestation true and evidence package is created.
5) Tenant acceptance: tenant signs acceptance form (digital) to confirm escrow.

HSM import / attestation checklist (ops)
- Validate attestation quote against expected hardware model and firmware fingerprint.
- Verify import token expiry and nonce match the manifest.
- Record request_id and generate evidence artifact id immediately.
- Avoid logging any import blob content; store only sha256 digest in logs.

Sample control-plane API snippets (conceptual)
- Import key (curl):
  curl -X POST https://kms.redwood.example/v1/keys/import \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"tenant_id":"tn-5101","import_blob":"BASE64_BLOB","manifest_id":"m-20260219-0001"}'

- Rotate key (curl):
  curl -X POST https://kms.redwood.example/v1/keys/ke-tn-5101-0007/rotate \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $OP_TOKEN" \
    -d '{"rotation_type":"scheduled","target_window":"2026-03-01T03:00:00Z"}'

Proof of destruction and retention
- Deletion in HSM is generally non-recoverable depending on hardware. For compliance we require:
  - Pre-deletion evidence bundle created and archived for retention policy (default 7 years for enterprise customers requesting proof).
  - Deletion log event that includes only key_id and deletion manifest id; deletion manifest contains HSM-provided deletion certificate (if available).

Compliance & legal notes
- For enterprise customers requiring BYOK with escrow, we must document chain-of-custody and provide attestation and evidence artifacts on request.
- Retention windows differ by contract; automations allow per-tenant overrides.

Runbooks & quick checks
- If rotation fails for >5% of tenants in a scheduled run: rollback new KEK version to previous state, unmark rewrap flag, and open incident with ops.
- If hsm_attestation false on import: quarantine import artifacts, revoke import token, require tenant to re-submit attestation after hardware check.
- If suspicious escrow download spike: revoke tenant API tokens and require rekeying with approval.

Open questions / action items
- Decide default retention period for evidence packages for BYOK customers vs non-BYOK customers (legal input needed).
- Determine whether escrow download events should automatically rotate KEKs after N suspicious downloads.
- Add RBAC v2 policy templates into repo for quick apply during onboarding (JIRA-SEC-7890).

Appendix: useful references
- Confluence: CONF-1234 Tenant Key Onboarding (detailed tenant forms and contract clauses)
- Repo: github.com/redwood-inference/kms-ops import/export scripts
- JIRA: JIRA-SEC-7890 (BYOK compliance backlog)
